rejected.title: The power of the Church
card: In medieval Western Europe, the Catholic Church was part of daily life for most people. It held great power as well as being the centre of faith.
Tithe
a tax paid to the Church. People gave a tenth of what they produced, such as crops or animals.
Monasteries
communities of monks or nuns. They copied books by hand and cared for the sick.
Excommunication
the Church could cast a person out of the Church. People believed this cut them off from God and salvation, so they feared it.
rejected.remember: The Church's power came from the tithe it collected, the monasteries it ran, and its right to cast people out.

a.q: What was a tithe in medieval Europe?
opts: A tenth of what people produced, paid to the Church
A tenth of a lord's land, given to his knights
A fine paid to the king for breaking a law
A tenth of a peasant's time, spent in the lord's fields
a.why: A tithe was a payment to the Church of a tenth of what people produced. Work in the lord's fields was a duty owed to a lord, not a payment to the Church.
a.clue: Think about who received the payment.

b.q: Why was excommunication a powerful tool for the medieval Church?
opts: People believed it cut them off from God and salvation
It took away a person's land and gave it to the Church
It sent the person to work in a monastery for life
It meant the person had to pay a larger tithe
b.why: People believed being cast out of the Church cut them off from God and salvation, so they feared it. The Church collected tithes for money, but excommunication was about a person's place in the Church, not a payment or a transfer of land.
b.clue: Think about what people believed the Church could give them.

a.q: Each harvest, a medieval farmer hands over one sack of grain for every ten he grows. What is this payment?
opts: A tithe, paid to the Church
Rent, paid to the lord of the manor
A fine, paid to the king's court
A tax, paid to the town's guild
a.why: A tithe was a payment to the Church of a tenth of what people produced, and one sack in ten is a tenth. Rent to the lord is tempting because peasants did owe their lord, but the tenth went to the Church.
a.clue: What fraction of the grain does the farmer hand over?

b.q: Agnes, a medieval villager, is told she will be cast out of the Church. Why would this frighten her most?
opts: People thought it cut them off from salvation
It took away a person's land and gave it to the Church
It sent the person to work in a monastery for life
It meant the person had to pay a larger tithe
b.why: Being cast out of the Church was called excommunication, and people believed it cut them off from God and salvation. It was about a person's place in the Church, not a payment, a loss of land or work in a monastery.
b.clue: Think about what people believed the Church could give them.

a.best: A tithe, paid to the Church

b.best: People thought it cut them off from salvation
